key_insight: A hybrid cross-modal attention model that combines mammograms with clinical data can improve early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings.
clinical_relevance: By using both imaging and structured patient information, the system may support more reliable screening where radiology expertise and data infrastructure are limited.
method: Trained a transformer-based cross-modal attention network on mammograms plus clinical features.
Used 2,560 mammogram images from 1,024 patients across four Ethiopian referral hospitals.
Compared performance against image-only baselines and tested robustness on low-quality images.
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and AUC 0.987, with only 3.2% degradation on low-quality images.
watch_item: Results come from a locally collected dataset, so broader validation across other populations and hospital workflows is still needed.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
